messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 — Customer Orbit (private VPC) reporting widespread 5xx on NLB ingress in us-west-2. Affected pool: orbit-dedicated-1. Paging @priya (oncall-sre) and @alex.

alex: Saw spike in 502/503 from the NLB logs, healthchecks showing intermittent failures around 11:41-11:46 UTC. No recent deploys from our side.

priya: Taking it — shifting pager. I'll check target health, SGs, and instance conntrack. @sam can you check DNS/Route53 weights and whether any traffic-steering jobs ran?

sam: Nothing in deploy logs or traffic jobs in last 3h. Quick check shows Route53 weight unchanged. Running target-health now.

alex: output from elbv2 describe-target-health (trimmed):
```
TargetId: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h
State: unhealthy (TCP/504)
Reason: TLS handshake failure / connection reset
UnhealthyCount: 12
```

customer-cx: Orbit support: errors started ~11:42 UTC. ~35-45% request failures on their prod traffic. Customer flagged as P1 for us.

priya: Hypothesis: intermittent connectivity between NLB and backend in private subnet — possibly SG drift or conntrack saturation on instances. Pulling sg for instances: sg-0a9b8c7d

alex: SG shows very restrictive ephemeral egress for instance role; looks like a recently applied hardened rule is restricting NAT'ed connections. Also seeing conntrack near limit on a few hosts: `/proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count = 258900` (limit 262144).

priya: OK. Short-term mitigations: 1) shift portion of traffic to standby dedicated pool (orbit-standby-1) via Route53 weight change, 2) temporarily relax SG egress to allow established connections to NLB CIDR for 15m, 3) drain and rotate a few instances to clear conntrack. Will coordinate order to minimize impact.

sam: Applying weight change now — switching 30% to orbit-standby-1. TTL is 30s.

deploy-bot: Route53 change applied (change-id Z3ABCDEF6GHIJK). Status: PENDING -> INSYNC within 20s.

priya: Making SG change: running command to add rule allowing ephemeral egress to NLB subnets for port 1024-65535 (temporary). Command: `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0a9b8c7d --protocol tcp --port 1024-65535 --cidr 10.0.128.0/20`

alex: Started draining i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h and two other high-conn hosts. New instances provisioned and registered healthy. Conntrack on rotated hosts dropped below 10k after drain.

customer-cx: After reroute + instance rotation, Orbit reports errors down to ~6% within 3 minutes. They appreciate the fast mitigation — asking for root cause and long-term fix.

priya: Immediate state: Customer impact substantially reduced. Standby pool handling 30% with healthy backends. SG relaxed for 15m window; will revoke after stabilization. Long-term action items: increase conntrack_max in our AMI (and bake into autoscaling), add conntrack usage alert in console, audit recent SG hardening run that introduced restrictive egress rules, add NLB->instance established connection exception to hardened profile.

alex: Filing follow-up ticket and postmortem notes. Will include exact instance IDs, conntrack metrics, and SG change diff.

priya: Handoff: I'll continue follow-up triage tomorrow with infra and security. Oncall clear in 15m if no regressions. Great job team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident SEV2 downgraded to SEV3 (mitigated) — follow-up ticket REDWOOD-5421 created for root cause and remediation.
